stem: The components of food that our body needs are called __________.
solution: Nutrients are the components of food — carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals — required by the body.

stem: Carbohydrates mainly provide __________ to the body.
solution: Carbohydrates are the body's chief source of energy.

stem: Proteins are called 'body-building' nutrients because they help in __________.
options: growth and repair of body tissues
solution: Proteins build and repair body tissues and are essential for growth.

stem: Fats are important in the diet mainly because they __________.
options: provide a lot of energy and store it
solution: Fats are energy-rich nutrients; they provide and store energy and also cushion organs.

stem: Which test is used to detect the presence of starch in food?
solution: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch, indicating carbohydrate.

stem: A translucent oily patch left on paper after rubbing a food item indicates the presence of __________.
solution: Fats leave a greasy, translucent mark on paper — the oily-patch test.

stem: A diet that contains all nutrients in the right amounts is called a __________.
solution: A balanced diet supplies all the necessary nutrients (and roughage and water) in appropriate quantities.

stem: Vitamins and minerals are needed in __________ amounts but are essential for health.
solution: Vitamins and minerals are required in small quantities yet are vital for normal body functioning.

stem: The dietary fibre (roughage) in food __________.
options: helps in the movement of food through the intestine and prevents constipation
solution: Roughage adds bulk to food, aiding bowel movement and preventing constipation; it is not a nutrient source of energy.

stem: The deficiency disease caused by lack of vitamin C is __________.
solution: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, marked by bleeding, swollen gums.

stem: Night blindness is caused by the deficiency of __________.
solution: Lack of vitamin A causes night blindness (poor vision in dim light).

stem: The bone-related disease rickets in children is caused by the deficiency of __________.
solution: Vitamin D deficiency (needed for calcium absorption) causes rickets, leading to weak, deformed bones.

stem: The deficiency disease beriberi is caused by lack of __________.
solution: Beriberi results from a deficiency of vitamin B1 (thiamine), affecting nerves and muscles.

stem: The disease goitre, marked by swelling of the neck, is caused by the deficiency of __________.
solution: Iodine deficiency causes goitre, an enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck.

stem: Anaemia, marked by weakness and pale skin, is commonly caused by the deficiency of __________.
solution: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; its deficiency causes anaemia.

stem: The mineral needed for strong bones and teeth is __________.
solution: Calcium is essential for the formation and strength of bones and teeth.

stem: The disease caused by severe deficiency of proteins, especially in children, is __________.
solution: Kwashiorkor results from severe protein deficiency, causing swelling and stunted growth.

stem: Which of the following foods is a rich source of proteins?
solution: Pulses, eggs, fish, meat and milk are rich protein sources.

stem: Which of the following is a rich source of carbohydrates?
solution: Cereals like rice and wheat, and tubers like potato, are rich in carbohydrates.

stem: Which of the following provides a rich source of fats?
solution: Ghee, butter, oils, nuts and oilseeds are rich in fats.

stem: Citrus fruits like oranges and lemons are a good source of __________.
solution: Citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C (ascorbic acid).

stem: The main source of vitamin D for the human body, apart from food, is __________.
solution: The body makes vitamin D when the skin is exposed to sunlight.

stem: Which nutrient is needed by the body in the largest amount by weight, apart from water?
solution: Carbohydrates typically form the largest energy-giving portion of the diet by weight, apart from water.

stem: Overeating and eating too much fatty and sugary food can lead to __________.
solution: Excess intake of fats and sugars can cause obesity and associated diseases such as diabetes and heart problems.

stem: Which of these is the best example of 'mindful eating'?
options: Eating a balanced meal in the right quantity and avoiding waste
Eating as much junk food as possible
Eating only one type of food
solution: Mindful eating means choosing balanced, adequate food, eating in moderation and reducing food waste.

stem: Water is important in our diet because it __________.
options: helps in digestion, transport of substances and removal of wastes
solution: Water aids digestion, transports nutrients and wastes, and regulates body temperature, though it is not an energy nutrient.

stem: Cooking food is useful because it __________.
options: makes food easier to digest and kills harmful germs
solution: Cooking softens food for easier digestion and destroys many harmful microbes, though excessive cooking can lose some vitamins.

stem: Boiling vegetables for a very long time is not advisable because it __________.
solution: Prolonged boiling destroys heat- and water-sensitive vitamins such as vitamin C.

stem: A person eating only rice for every meal is likely to suffer because the diet is __________.
options: unbalanced and lacking proteins, vitamins and minerals
solution: Rice provides mainly carbohydrates; a rice-only diet lacks proteins, several vitamins and minerals, making it unbalanced.

stem: Green leafy vegetables are especially valued in the diet because they are rich in __________.
solution: Green leafy vegetables supply vitamins, minerals (like iron) and dietary fibre.

stem: Milk is considered a nearly complete food for infants because it contains __________.
options: proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals
solution: Milk supplies proteins, fats, carbohydrates (lactose), vitamins and minerals like calcium, making it nearly complete for infants.

stem: The energy value of food is commonly measured in __________.
solution: Food energy is expressed in calories or kilocalories.

stem: Which vitamin is important for healthy eyes and vision?
solution: Vitamin A is essential for good vision, especially in dim light.

stem: Which of the following pairs a deficiency disease with the correct nutrient lacking?
solution: Scurvy is due to lack of vitamin C. (Rickets–vitamin D, goitre–iodine, anaemia–iron are the correct matches for the others.)

stem: Roughage in the diet is mainly obtained from __________.
solution: Dietary fibre (roughage) comes from plant foods — fruits, vegetables and whole grains.

stem: The staple food of a region depends largely on __________.
options: the crops that grow there and local eating habits
the colour of the soil only
solution: Staple foods (like rice, wheat, maize) depend on which crops grow well locally and on regional dietary habits.

stem: Which of the following habits helps maintain a healthy body?
options: Eating balanced meals, drinking enough water and being physically active
solution: A balanced diet, adequate water and physical activity together support good health.

stem: Sprouting of pulses and grains before eating is beneficial because it __________.
options: increases their vitamin content and makes them easier to digest
solution: Germination (sprouting) raises the vitamin content and digestibility of pulses and grains.

stem: Which of these is a food adulterant problem that mindful choices try to avoid?
options: Mixing cheaper or harmful substances into food to increase quantity
solution: Adulteration is the addition of inferior or harmful substances to food; mindful, informed eating helps avoid it.

stem: Fresh fruits are a better source of vitamins than fruit juices left standing for long because __________.
options: some vitamins are lost on exposure to air and time
solution: Vitamins like vitamin C degrade with exposure to air and time, so fresh fruit often retains more than long-standing juice.

stem: A diet deficient in iodine, common in some hilly regions, is often corrected by using __________.
solution: Iodised salt is used to prevent iodine-deficiency disorders such as goitre.

stem: Which of the following statements about a balanced diet is correct?
options: It varies with age, sex and level of physical activity
It is the same for everyone regardless of activity
solution: The right balanced diet differs by age, gender, and how physically active a person is.

stem: Excess of a fat-soluble vitamin can be harmful because such vitamins __________.
options: are stored in the body and can accumulate to toxic levels
solution: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored in the body and can build up to harmful levels if taken in excess.

stem: The best way to reduce food wastage at home is to __________.
options: cook and serve only what is needed and store leftovers properly
cook far more than required daily
solution: Planning portions, serving what is needed and storing leftovers reduces food waste — a part of mindful eating.

stem: Which nutrient class does NOT provide energy to the body?
solution: Minerals (and vitamins) are protective/regulatory nutrients and do not directly provide energy, unlike carbohydrates, fats and proteins.

stem: The process by which the body breaks down food to absorb nutrients is called __________.
solution: Digestion breaks food into simpler substances that the body can absorb and use.

stem: Which meal habit best supports steady energy through the day?
options: Eating regular, balanced meals including breakfast
Eating one huge meal only at night
solution: Regular balanced meals, including breakfast, provide steady energy and better health.

stem: Traditional Indian thalis are often nutritionally sound because they combine __________.
options: cereals, pulses, vegetables, curd and other items giving varied nutrients
solution: A typical thali combines cereals, pulses, vegetables, curd and more, together supplying a balance of nutrients.

stem: The nutrient that helps in blood clotting and is found in green leafy vegetables is associated with vitamin __________.
solution: Vitamin K, found in green leafy vegetables, is needed for normal blood clotting.

stem: Excess consumption of sugary drinks is linked to __________.
solution: High sugar intake promotes tooth decay and unhealthy weight gain.

stem: The habit of washing hands before eating helps prevent __________.
solution: Washing hands removes germs and helps prevent food-borne infections and diseases.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body' is that:
options: a balanced diet in the right quantity, eaten thoughtfully and without waste, keeps the body healthy
eating anything in any amount is fine
solution: The chapter teaches that health depends on eating a balanced diet in proper amounts, chosen mindfully and with minimal waste.
